answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with staked identity: every agent must lock real funds behind its identity before acting, and the lock grows with its track record. A swarm of clones then stops being cheap, since each new account demands fresh capital plus proven history, so a thousand fake agents must post a thousand real bonds. If any member misbehaves, the whole cluster and its guarantors are slashed together. Honest agents collect a share of those slashes, like nectar to loyal actors, while attackers bleed umber losses. Any gain is a rare comet of luck, rarely worth the stake.
